clue.text: Madly stamp piles of unoriginal writing

indicators.note: madly says the letters of the two words that follow are thrown into a wild new order

explanation.surface: Someone furiously stamps on piles of plagiarised or second-hand writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges the ten letters of STAMP PILES; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript scraped and written over keeps traces of earlier text, so its writing is not the first on the page.

clue.text: Situation of one that is deaf

definitions.meaning: a situation in the sense of a job or position held
the simile 'deaf as a ...' makes the wooden upright the standard of deafness

explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job or station; and the saying 'as deaf as a post' names the timber upright as the deaf one.

clue.text: See about learning this

parts.note: lo is an old interjection meaning look or see
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: An invitation to look into the details of what you are studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional knowledge handed down is a body of learning.

clue.text: Its projects were wonderfully picturesque

parts.note: 'projects' is a verb: an old device that threw pictures on a screen, and 'wonderfully' points to the first word of its name

explanation.surface: Praise for some architectural or planning schemes that turned out beautifully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projects' looks like a noun meaning schemes; it is the verb, throwing images onto a screen, and those images were 'pictures'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian slide projector cast painted pictures, its first word meaning wonderful or enchanting.

clue.text: Universal system this of central heating

definitions.text: Universal system this of central heating

parts.words: Universal system this of central heating
parts.note: the system in the universe whose central body heats the planets around it, named after the sun

explanation.surface: Advertising copy for a boiler that will heat any house from the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central heating' reads as home plumbing, but it is the sun at the centre warming the planets of the system.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names our planetary system, heated by the star at its centre.

clue.text: Made to look silly by a K.O.

definitions.meaning: made to seem foolish or stupid
a knockout leaves a boxer stunned and unconscious

explanation.definitionFit: Stupid or pointless in one sense, and unconscious in the other, as a knockout leaves a fighter.

clue.text: Slave-princess needs top U.S. lawyer

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or top
DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: An enslaved royal requires the best American attorney to win her freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: AI (A1, first-class) plus DA; 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Verdi's opera is an Ethiopian princess held as a slave in Egypt.

clue.text: Founder perhaps rules with the proverbial rod

definitions.meaning: a founder here is one who casts metal in a foundry, not one who establishes something
the saying 'rule with a rod of iron' describes a stern master of that metal

explanation.definitionFit: A foundry owner making metal goods is one example of a founder; and someone ruling with a rod of iron is a master by that metal.

clue.text: Army dressings ?

parts.note: soldiers 'dress' their ranks by lining up straight, so dressings are not bandages but straightened lines

explanation.surface: A question about military bandages or uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressings' suggests bandages or uniforms; on parade, to dress is to straighten the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks means bringing soldiers into straight lines, which are arrangements in a row.

clue.text: A child's horse, a novice, in trainer's line-out is not keeping up

indicators.note: in places the horse and the learner inside the racehorse trainer's line of horses

parts.note: a racehorse trainer's stable of horses is called his string
gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, shortened to GG
L is a learner, as on the L-plate of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A youngster's pony and a beginner fall behind at the back of a trainer's line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A, GG and L go inside STRING, a racing trainer's string of horses; 'out' is a link word. The definition is a verb phrase matching the -ing form.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagging behind the rest means failing to keep pace.

clue.text: Note retreat of West African tribe to desert

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale

indicators.note: a retreat is a drawing back, so the tribe's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: the Ibo (Igbo) are a people of Nigeria

explanation.surface: A Nigerian people's withdrawal into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat of' turns IBO into OBI, which follows G; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The great arid region spanning Mongolia and northern China is a desert.

clue.text: How dreadful, a foreign wine season without one!

parts.note: Wein is German for wine

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the season wraps round the letter for one

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An exclamation of horror at some foreign wine that lacks a vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: SPRING goes round I. 'How' is a link word, and 'dreadful' is meant in its root sense of inspiring dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fills you with dread or reverential fear is fearsome in the old sense.

clue.text: Mrs. Will of Sherwood Forest or Rome

definitions.meaning: Will Scarlet is one of Robin Hood's band in Sherwood Forest, so his wife would bear his surname
Protestant polemic named the Roman Catholic Church after the harlot of the Book of Revelation

explanation.definitionFit: The wife of Robin Hood's outlaw Will would be a Scarlet lady; and old Protestant writers called the Church of Rome the Whore of Babylon by this name.

clue.text: Is it the sound of rats opting out of the race ?

definitions.text: Is it the sound of rats
definitions.meaning: the noise of claws scraping behind a skirting board
a horse or runner withdrawn before the start is said to be scratched

explanation.definitionFit: Clawing noises are what rats make behind a wall; and withdrawing an entrant from a contest is called scratching it.

clue.text: Party speeches giving birth to technological revolution ?

parts.note: Lab is the standard abbreviation for the British Labour Party
oratory is the art or practice of making speeches

explanation.surface: Political speeches from the left producing a modern industrial revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: the place where scientific work brings new technology into being.
explanation.definitionFit: Research rooms are where scientists and engineers produce the innovations that drive technical change.

clue.text: He must be a curmudgeon to decry teacher's present

parts.note: to crab is to criticise or find fault
an apple is the traditional gift a pupil brings for the teacher

explanation.surface: Only a grouch would sneer at the gift a child gives the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The sour wild fruit stands for a sour-tempered person, so 'he must be a curmudgeon' describes one; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sour wild fruit is used figuratively of a sour, grumpy person.

clue.text: One of the main hazards was said to be a hired eavesdropper

indicators.note: says the eavesdropper's description is spoken, giving words that sound like the answer

parts.note: a paid detective is a private eye, so a hired listener is a private ear

explanation.surface: A claim that some danger at sea was in fact a paid spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, an old poetic sense; armed private ships licensed to seize enemy merchant ships were a danger there.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed ships commissioned to capture enemy vessels were a peril of the high seas, called the main.

clue.text: Children joined in argument

definitions.meaning: to join ... is to take up a point of dispute

explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are one's descendants in legal language; and in the idiom 'join issue' it is the point in dispute.

clue.text: Jack in ? Not exactly

definitions.meaning: the question asks where the boxer Jack is: in a bout, a boxing match

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer such as Jack Dempsey fights in a bout, so 'Jack in ?' asks for 'a bout'; and roughly means approximately.

clue.text: Is ten in Jan, and won't take " No " for an answer

definitions.text: won't take " No " for an answer

indicators.note: the words is and ten are placed in the abbreviation the month gives

parts.note: in a letter written in January, the current month is called inst., short for instant
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who demands that a date be fixed for the tenth of January.
explanation.walkthrough: Old business letters wrote 'the 10th inst.' for the tenth of this month, so January, if it is the present month, is INST; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps demanding and refuses a refusal is persistent in a demand.

clue.text: Presidency gives honour to flying ability

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order
skill at piloting an aircraft is airmanship

explanation.surface: Being made president brings a decoration to a skilled pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award; 'gives' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding the post of president of a meeting or board is presiding over it.

clue.text: Oceanographic features turn up at such a rate

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the deeps are the deepest trenches of the ocean

explanation.surface: Seabed features appearing at a surprising frequency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses DEEPS; 'at such a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace or velocity is the rate at which something moves.

clue.text: All in order, some being flat on the floor

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Everything tidy, with some people lying flat on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes part of 'alL IN Order'. The definition is a cryptic description of a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum is a floor covering, so it lies flat on the floor.

clue.text: A girl sent up a cry of distress

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending the name upward reads it backwards

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A girl shot upward and let out a scream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns SAL into LAS after A; 'a' before the definition is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret is a cry of distress.

clue.text: Trickster admits his image

parts.note: the trickster speaking of himself says I
a con is a con man, a swindler

explanation.surface: A swindler confesses to a portrait of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: What the trickster admits is 'I con': the I is his own self, followed by CON; 'admits' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious picture or any symbolic representation is an image.

clue.text: Like a little of what you fancy

definitions.text: Like a little of what you fancy

parts.words: Like a little of what you fancy
parts.note: the saying 'a little of what you fancy does you good' describes something that is good for you

explanation.surface: A gentle endorsement of small indulgences.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall saying 'a little of what you fancy does you good' completes the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing someone good is being advantageous or wholesome.

clue.text: Blokes in hospital

explanation.definitionFit: Men are fellows; and Guy's Hospital is a famous London hospital.

clue.text: Astonishing to dig after gold back among the devout

indicators.note: among places the reversed gold and the dig inside the word for the devout

parts.note: the devout are pious

indicators.note: after puts the dig behind the reversed gold
back says the heraldic word for gold is read from end to start

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Amazing how readily the religious go digging for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OR into RO; 'after' puts DIG after it, and 'among' sets RODIG inside PIOUS; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable in size or degree means amazing or marvellous.
